$comment: Machine-readable acceptance ledger (ТЗ 10/10 rev2 §22, §18.3). One entry per program milestone: status, requirement/evidence lists, blocking issues, waivers and the accepted commit. A milestone whose status is NOT 'accepted' must not be treated as a completed stage: downstream milestones may proceed only with evidence that this ledger records. No user consent, debug mode or high-risk grant can override a blocked requirement. Ordering gate (audit 'CI gate blocking M2 while M1.status != accepted'): a milestone may only be marked 'accepted' when EVERY earlier milestone is 'accepted'; scripts/check-milestone-gates.mjs --check enforces this in CI. Waivers must be limited ADR waivers: the gate validates by/date/severity/expiry/reason/adr, rejects automated actors and P0 waivers. Evidence must be structured and reproducible (test-run: command + commit in HEAD ancestry; ci: ciRun URL; artifact: path) — bare strings are rejected.

policy.comment: Strict sequential ordering: shipping work for a later milestone while a predecessor is not accepted fails the CI gate (scripts/check-milestone-gates.mjs). Formal acceptance additionally requires every earlier milestone accepted, an existing acceptedCommit in HEAD ancestry, empty or formally waived (non-P0) blockingIssues and non-empty structured evidence. THIS branch (m1-w1-security-clean) carries ONLY M1 work — M2/M3/M4 are recorded as pending with no deliveredCommit, so the gate is green except for M1 awaiting its human acceptance.

m2-contentReview.scope: read-only review of crates/runtime-kernel/src/generation.rs (2208 lines), prompt.rs (647 lines), provider-openai-compat, packages/contracts/src/wire, and the M2 test files at 2c5e156 on m1-w1-security (source for pr-kernel-golden).
m2-contentReview.finding: M2 generation content satisfies ТЗ §8.3/§9.2/§9.3/§9.4: CAS revision state machine with lost-CAS reaction (cancel wins, terminal wins, else retry — never blind retry); durable immutable step journal with per-run gapless sequence and idempotency keys (turn-{seq}/tool-call-{id}/tool-result-{id}); WaitingForTool is a durable pending_tool_call_json marker committed with the tool_call step in ONE transaction (no open DB transaction held); tool calls validated against the registry (TOOL_NOT_FOUND/TOOL_ARGS_INVALID) with MAX_TOOL_CALLS loop budget (TOOL_LOOP_LIMIT); exactly-once completed = assistant message INSERT + status CAS + terminal event in one transaction; stale tool result rejected (TOOL_RESULT_STALE); cancel re-read at every emit boundary and on waiting runs; crash recovery marks expired-lease runs 'interrupted' (recoverable); provider secrets resolved at execution time via the SecretResolver seam with fail-closed no-resolver policy (ProviderError::Unavailable, no plaintext fallback) and used only in the Authorization header, never stored/logged.
m2-contentReview.tests: crates/runtime-kernel/tests/tool_loop.rs 10 cases: golden tool round trip, unregistered tool fails, invalid arguments fail, stale tool result rejected, tool result on non-waiting run is stale, cancel on waiting run finalizes cancelled, retry on waiting run is a state conflict, tool loop limit fails the run, crash at wait reopens and resumes, empty registry yields no tools. Plus generation.rs, providers_openai.rs, contracts wire_corpus.rs, built-in-providers conformance.rs, adapters/remote-http/tests/generation_stream.rs.

interrupted runs are an explicit recoverable terminal state; resume is a UI/user retry, not automatic continuation
streaming runs on a synchronous writer thread with an mpsc channel; backpressure is EmitStatus::Stop at step boundaries, not an async stream
